title: Queue Dynamics and Latency Correlator Handbook
author: Evan Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This handbook describes the design, instrumentation, and operational playbooks for the Queue Dynamics & Latency Correlator (QDLC) — a lightweight service and analysis pattern we run alongside the serving runtime to detect, attribute, and triage queue-induced latency across kernel, scheduling, and KV-cache interactions. It is intended for on-call SREs, runtime engineers, and performance-focused platform owners.

Scope: correlating queue depth, per-request kernel activity, execution priority, and tail latency across host, shard, and tenant dimensions. Does NOT replace detailed kernel profiling (see profiling-playbook).

Why this exists
- Queues are the most common multi-tenant root cause for increased P50/P95/P99 token latency.
- Pure CPU/GPU kernel traces are high-fidelity but expensive; QDLC uses aggregated probes, cheap traces, and causal correlation heuristics to speed diagnosis.

Signal sources and tags
- Metrics (Prometheus): request_queue_length, request_enqueue_time_seconds, request_dequeue_time_seconds, kernel_dispatch_time_seconds, kvcache_miss_rate, tenant_priority, kernel_backpressure_counter
- Traces: span names: qdlc.enqueue, qdlc.dequeue, kernel.dispatch, kernel.exec, kvcache.lookup
- Logs: structured events with fields: request_id, shard_id, tenant_id, model_variant, seq_len, prefetch_hint
- Telemetry tags: host_zone, gpu_type, kernel_version, experiment_flag, admission_controller_profile

Architecture and dataflow
1. Ingress probe: lightweight sampler in the request front-door that emits an enqueue event with timestamp and classification (read-only, streaming, chat) and attaches a short id.
2. Queue aggregator: per-host, in-memory rolling histogram of queue lengths and per-class enqueue/dequeue latencies. Exposes Prometheus metrics and a small local HTTP API for sample dumps.
3. Correlator service: periodically pulls aggregated histograms + sampled traces and runs attribution heuristics (see "Attribution heuristics" below).
4. Notifier / dashboard: alerts (PagerDuty + Slack) for policy breaches and a visual timeline in the runtime observability dashboard.

Data model (flat)
- sample_id: short hex
- ts_start, ts_end: epoch seconds
- queue_len_history: CSV of (sec, len)
- class_breakdown: JSON string (class -> count) (bounded to 1k chars)
- kernel_hints: list of kernel names separated by ';'

Attribution heuristics (brief)
- Temporal overlap: if a spike in queue_len_history correlates with rising P95 and majority of dequeues are > T_dequeue_threshold, attribute to queueing.
- Kernel sensitivity: use per-kernel sensitivity index (S_k) from kernel-sensitivity catalog; if dequeues show kernel.exec spans with high S_k and queue lag, attribute to kernel-induced slowdowns amplified by queueing.
- Tenant stigma: if tenant_priority==low and tokenized share > 30% of dequeues during the spike, escalate to tenancy throttling candidate.

Operational SLOs and alerting thresholds
- P99 request enqueued-to-dequeue time: target < 40ms (SLO: 99.9% under 100ms).
- Request queue length per host: soft limit 200, hard limit 500.
- Queue-induced tail latency alert: fires when P99 enqueue->dequeue > 150ms AND host queue_len > 250 for 30s.

Runbook: investigation steps (ordered)
1) Triage the alert: check alert window, affected clusters, and sample request_ids.
2) Snapshot metrics: pull request_queue_length, kernel_dispatch_time_seconds, kvcache_miss_rate for host/shard/tenant for the 5m window. Use the provided queries below.
3) Correlate traces: request a QDLC sample dump (HTTP /qdlc/sample?window=5m&limit=50). Open spans for request_id with long dequeue times.
4) Classify root cause via checklist:
   a) If kvcache_miss_rate jumped > 3x concurrent with queue growth -> cache warmup/regression -> go to KV remediation.
   b) If kernel_dispatch_time increased per-dequeue and kernel sensitivity high -> kernel regression -> escalate to runtime-kernel oncall.
   c) If queue length high but dequeue times are low (bursty enqueue) -> upstream surge -> contact traffic source team and consider rate limiting.
   d) If low-priority tenants dominate dequeues -> apply immediate tenant-throttle policy and schedule quota adjustment.
5) Apply mitigation (see mitigation section).
6) Post-incident: create a triage note with sample ids, correlated kernel versions, and chosen mitigation. Attach to incident tracker and link to related pages.

Mitigation options (fast to medium)
1. Fast (within 60s): enable temporary tenant throttle via the admission controller: API call
   curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/adm-controller/throttle \
     -d '{"tenant_id":"TENANT","target_qps":100}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
2. Medium (2-15m): evict long-running low-priority requests: use the runtime eviction endpoint for shard: POST /runtime/shard/{shard}/evict?reason=queue_bust
3. Targeted (15-60m): reroute traffic to fallback model-variant with lower kernel sensitivity: update routing rule in rollout service.
4. Long-term: schedule kernel rollback or patch; update kernel-sensitivity index and re-run the fidelity suite.

KV remediation checklist
- Validate whether recent quantization/serialization changes increased miss rate.
- Check if prefetch hints are flowing and if warmup policy ran successfully.
- If miss rate persists, bump cache allocation for the shard for 1 hour and re-evaluate.

Configuration table (parameters operators may edit)
| parameter | default | safe range | notes |
|-----------|---------|------------|-------|
| qdlc.enqueue-sample-rate | 0.02 | 0.0 - 0.1 | Fraction of requests sampled at ingress |
| qdlc.aggregator-window-sec | 60 | 30 - 300 | Rolling window used for histograms |
| qdlc.alert-queue-hard-limit | 500 | 200 - 2000 | Hard queue length to trigger critical paths |
| qdlc.dequeue-latency-threshold-ms | 150 | 50 - 1000 | Used in queue+latency alert rule |

Example queries
- Prometheus (host-level queue P99):
  sum by (host) (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_dequeue_time_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, host)))
- Compare queue vs kernel dispatch:
  increase(request_queue_length[5m]) > 0 and increase(kernel_dispatch_time_seconds_sum[5m]) / increase(kernel_dispatch_time_seconds_count[5m]) > 0.02

Sample trace annotation pattern (recommended conventions)
- qdlc.enqueue: attributes {"class":"streaming","seq_len":128,"tenant_id":"t-123"}
- kernel.exec: attributes {"kernel_name":"attn_fused_v2","lat_ms":12,"kernel_version":"k1.4.3"}
- qdlc.dequeue: attributes {"dequeue_lat_ms":45,"queue_pos":14}

Testing and rollout guidance
- Feature gate: qdlc.enabled default off for new regions. Rollout plan: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with 24h observation windows.
- Canary tests: run synthetic microbursts (see benchmarking suite) against canary host and assert enqueue->dequeue P99 < 80ms.

Ownership and escalation
- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime / performance (oncall alias: runtime-perf@redwood.example.com)
- Escalation: runtime-kernel team after 10m of undiagnosed elevated dequeue latency or if kernel.exec spans show >25% regression in mean latency.

Post-incident analysis template (required fields)
1. Summary (one sentence)
2. Window (start, end)
3. Affected tenants and models
4. Root cause hypothesis and evidence (metrics, traces)
5. Mitigations applied and timestamps
6. Action items and owners (with due dates)

Related pages and references
- Runtime telemetry sampling guide (for guidance on safe sample rates)
- Kernel sensitivity index (living document)
- Canary workload definitions (benchmarking suite)

Appendix: debugging commands and helpers
- Dump aggregator state (host): curl http://localhost:9081/qdlc/debug/state | jq '.'
- Trigger a sample dump: curl http://localhost:9081/qdlc/debug/dump?duration=30s&limit=200 -H 'Accept: application/json' > dump.json
- Local replay of sample (developer laptop): python tools/replay_qdlc.py --input dump.json --prometheus-push-url http://localhost:9091/metrics

Notes and future work
- Add a tenant-aware admission-controller policy that preemptively slows low-priority streams when kernel sensitivity on the host crosses a configurable threshold.
- Integrate with runtime Optimize recommendations to auto-adjust qdlc.sample_rate based on cost budgets.

Authors and contributors: Evan Chen (owner), Priya Nair (observability), Liam O'Connor (runtime).
